correctness.rationale: Reconstructed normalization to level-preserving maps via pointwise comparable moves on crown minima/maxima. Normalized moves coincide with spur replacement of alternating closed walks in K_(r,s). Redundant spur sliding identifies nonmaximal cyclically reduced words up to rotation, while a spur-free maximal-length map has no allowable move; Burnside yields the stated totient necklace sum and the isolated count. Independently built connected components of normalized-move graphs and verified (m,r,s)=(3,3,4),(4,2,3),(4,3,3),(5,2,2),(5,2,3),(6,2,2),(6,2,3); finite tests corroborate, not replace all-m proof.

value.rationale: Maps between natural minimal finite circle models and complete height-two finite posets have distinct homotopy components, so an exact structural necklace classification and sharp no-slack isolation boundary are useful topological invariants beyond routine map counting. The three-parameter result extends known four-point target specializations.

limitations: Unbased finite-space homotopy only for crown→complete height-two targets, m,r,s≥2.
